'''Orien Randolph Greene II''' (born February 4, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. His first two professional seasons were spent with the NBA's [[Boston Celtics]] and [[Indiana Pacers]], respectively.<ref name=signswithkings/> He played briefly with the [[Sacramento Kings]] in 2007,<ref name=waivedbykings>{{cite news| url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/2007-11-15-891186592_x.htm | work=USA Today | title=Sacramento Kings waive guard Orien Greene | date=November 15, 2007}}</ref> and with the [[New Jersey Nets]] in 2011.

== College career ==
A highly touted prospect coming out of high school, the {{convert|6|ft|4|in|m|adj=on}} [[point guard]] originally chose to attend the [[University of Florida]], his hometown college. However, after a couple of years Greene became dissatisfied with his playing time and decided to transfer to the [[University of Louisiana at Lafayette]] where he became known in the [[Sun Belt Conference]] for his aggressive play, winning the Defensive Player of the Year award his senior season.

However, in 2007, an NCAA investigation found that Greene had relied on 15 hours of correspondence courses taken through another institution in order to remain eligible for the 2004 spring semester and the entire 2004–05 academic year. NCAA rules do not allow student-athletes to use correspondence courses taken from another institution to remain eligible. According to the NCAA, this was an "obvious error" that should have been caught right away, but the school's then-compliance coordinator director of academic services and registrar all failed to catch it. When school officials learned about the violations, they vacated every game in which Greene participated—43 games in all, including NCAA tournament appearances in 2004 and 2005—and scrubbed Greene's records from the books. The NCAA accepted Louisiana-Lafayette's penalties and also imposed two years' probation.<ref>[https://web1.ncaa.org/LSDBi/exec/miSearch?miSearchSubmit=publicReport&key=633&publicTerms=THIS%20PHRASE%20WILL%20NOT%20BE%20REPEATED 2007 Louisiana-Lafayette infractions report]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/friv/forfeits.cgi|title=Forfeits and Vacated Games}}</ref>

==Professional career ==
Greene was drafted in [[2005 NBA draft]] with the 53rd overall pick by the [[Boston Celtics]].

Greene began his pro career as backup to [[Delonte West]]. His status as the backup point guard was cemented by a season-ending injury to [[Dan Dickau]] and the trade of [[Marcus Banks]] to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].

On March 29, 2006, Greene was suspended by the Boston Celtics for one game after he was charged with driving his [[sport utility vehicle]] at more than {{convert|90|mi/h|km/h|abbr=on}} on a street in suburban [[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]].

On June 30, 2006, Greene was waived by the Boston Celtics. He was claimed off waivers by the [[Indiana Pacers]], and played for their 2006–2007 team.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Montieth|first1=Mark|title=Greene joins Pacers for summer league|url=http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20060710/SPORTS04/607100377/1088|website=Indianapolis Star|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060820144403/http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20060710%2FSPORTS04%2F607100377%2F1088|archive-date=August 20, 2006|date=July 10, 2006|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Greene was used very sparingly in his season with the Pacers. He played in only 41 games, averaging 6.2 minutes per game; quite a drop off compared to playing in all but 2 games the previous year with the Celtics and averaging 15.4 minutes per game. The Pacers brought in [[Darrell Armstrong]] (from Dallas) and [[Keith McLeod]] (from Golden State) to compete with Greene for minutes at point guard. With [[Jamaal Tinsley]] holding the starting position, Greene fell to fourth on the depth chart, which resulted in very little playing time. Greene signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]] on August 30, 2007.<ref name=signswithkings>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20070528102325/http://www.sacbee.com/100/story/351634.html|title=Theus completes his staff}}, posted August 30, 2007</ref> He was waived by the Kings November 15, 2007 after playing just 7 games.<ref name=waivedbykings/>

Greene signed a three-month contract with the Australian National Basketball League's New Zealand Breakers in late November 2007. He was signed to replace [[Wayne Turner (basketball)|Wayne Turner]], who was out for the season.<ref name=signswithbreakers>{{cite news |url=http://tvnz.co.nz/view/page/536641/1464645 |title=Breakers sign replacement from NBA |date=November 27, 2007 |work=[[One Sport]] |access-date=November 1, 2011}}</ref>

In 2010 Greene has been banned for two years for trying to dupe drug testers, backdated to March 12, 2009.<ref>[http://www.usada.org/usada-and-the-netherlands-anti-doping-authority-partner-to-uncover-tampering-scheme/ USADA And The Netherlands Anti-Doping Authority Partner To Uncover Tampering Scheme usada.org 8 June 2010]</ref>

He later played for the [[Utah Flash]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/index.jsp?player=orien_greene Orien Greene]. D-League profile].</ref> On February 1, 2011, Greene re-joined the NBA as he signed a 10-day contract with the New Jersey Nets. Afterwards, he rejoined the Flash.

On November 10, 2011, Orien Greene signed to play basketball for the [[Halifax Rainmen]] of the [[National Basketball League of Canada|NBL]]. Shortly afterwards, he joined the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the NBA D-League.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/111215oriengreene.html D-FENDERS ACQUIRE ORIEN GREENE]</ref>

In October 2012, Greene signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11038 |title=Bucks add Eddie Gill, Orien Greene, Mustapha Farrakhan, Alando Tucker to training camp roster |access-date=October 2, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905194618/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11038 |archive-date=September 5, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was waived by the team later that month.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11306 |title=Bucks waive Mustapha Farrakhan, Eddie Gill, Orien Greene, Alando Tucker |access-date=October 27, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304060800/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11306 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Later that month, he was re-acquired by the Los Angeles D-Fenders.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html Full List of 2012 Returning, Affiliate and Local Tryout Players Invited to NBA D-League Training Camps] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218094230/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html |date=December 18, 2015 }}</ref> On February 25, 2013, Greene was traded to the [[Reno Bighorns]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/130225_jordan.html D-Fenders Trade for Jerome Jordan] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130227042006/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/130225_jordan.html |date=February 27, 2013 }}</ref>

In October 2013, he joined Al Alhy Benghazi of Libya.

In December 2014, he joined [[Fuerza Regia]] of the Mexican [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Debutará con Fuerza Regia el ex NBA Orien Green|url=http://dominio.fm/debutara-con-fuerza-regia-el-ex-nba-orien-green/|access-date=February 17, 2015|work=dominio.fm|date=December 1, 2014|language=es|archive-date=February 17, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217153816/http://dominio.fm/debutara-con-fuerza-regia-el-ex-nba-orien-green/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On December 31, 2016, Greene signed with [[Guaros de Lara (basketball)|Guaros de Lara]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]].<ref>[https://twitter.com/GuarosOficial/status/815218159678607361 El alero Orien Greene será nuestro tercer importado de cara a la Liga de Las Américas y la LPB]</ref>
